title: Reduce streaming token latency: optimize token loop, flush cadence, and backpressure
author: Priya Nair
description: Context: Customers reported tail latency spikes and token-level jitter in streaming responses under mixed workloads. Previous fixes reduced mean latency but left pathologies related to the token emission loop, flush cadence heuristics, and backpressure propagation across the serving pipeline. Motivation: Improve token-level latency and smooth streaming throughput without regressing throughput or memory usage. Approach: 1) Token loop: refactor the streaming token dispatch loop to decouple scheduling from transport flush cadence; replace per-request timers with a central low-overhead scheduler that groups ready tokens into micro-flush windows. 2) Flush cadence: introduce adaptive flush windows that use recent inter-token timing (EWMA) and model batch occupancy signals to decide 1ms/5ms/10ms micro-windows, reducing unnecessary small writes while avoiding large latency spikes. 3) Backpressure: add explicit backpressure signals from the transport layer to the serving runtime to prevent token queue growth; integrate with existing continuous-batching controller to shed or throttle lower-priority requests. 4) KV cache eviction order: small change to prioritize hot keys and reduce misses during bursty regeneration. 5) Kernel scheduling hint: expose a lightweight hint for the kernel selector to preferentially schedule small next-token kernels during streaming-heavy slices. Benchmark results: microbenchmarks on c6g and A100 clusters show median token latency reduction of 28%, P95 reduction of 42% under mixed infer/load scenarios; end-to-end streaming throughput unchanged within 3% and memory delta <2%. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag streaming_adaptive_flush; staged rollout to 10% canary then 50% then full after 48h metrics check. Backports: recommend backport to release-2026-02 if no regressions. See linked linear tasks for evaluation prompts and perf dashboards.
commits: Refactor streaming token loop to centralized scheduler (pri: reduce per-request timers)
Add adaptive flush cadence with EWMA-based window sizing
Propagate transport-level backpressure to batcher and add throttling path
KV cache hot-key re-priority during streaming bursts
Expose kernel scheduling hint and small kernel fast-path

review_comments: Ethan Kim: Can you explain why centralizing the timers doesn't add contention under high concurrency? Author: The scheduler uses sharded run queues and per-core timers to avoid contention; added microbench in tests showing no lock scaling issues.

María López: The EWMA window seems sensitive to sudden load changes. Can we add a floor/ceiling? Author: Added min/max bounds (1ms/20ms) and a forced immediate flush on end-of-stream or model termination signals.

Dmitri Petrov: Backpressure propagation risks head-of-line blocking for higher-priority requests. Author: Batching controller was extended to maintain priority lanes; lower-priority lanes get throttled and shed first, documented in the PR.
CI bot: integration-streaming failed on first run due to flaky timer in test harness. Author: Fixed test to use deterministic clock; re-ran and all checks passed.

release_notes: Reduce token-level streaming latency by ~28% median and ~42% P95 via centralized token scheduler, adaptive flush cadence, and improved backpressure. No throughput regression observed. Feature is behind runtime flag streaming_adaptive_flush and will be rolled out gradually. Backport recommended to release-2026-02.
